newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares seen riding even higher on fund flow.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares seen riding even higher on fund flow.

text.p: A fast and furious flow of cash into the Russian stock market, which has pushed up stocks over 40 percent this month, is not stopping and neither will the Russian bull market, traders and analysts said Friday.
"Senior decisions have been taken on a senior level with these big funds," said Lars Bergstrom, Managing Director of Alfred Berg investment bank in Moscow.
"The Americans are definitely ahead in terms of (investment) volumes, but I think we will see the big European money coming in later this year."
Daily volumes topped $75 million this week, three times the level previously considered healthy, testifying to an inflow of new money.
Shares hit yet another record Friday, with the Russian Trading System 24-share index ending 1.21 percent higher at 291.98 against 189.85 on Dec. 25.
Utility Mosenergo, the bellwether of the market, which traded at $1.580 midday Friday, closed at 97.8 cents on Dec. 25.
But the Russian market, which the International Finance Corp. said returned 156 percent last year as the world's best performing emerging market, is still considered cheap.

"A couple of leading stocks (now) have price-to-sales ratios that on the surface look comparable to the West, but they don't reflect growth potential," said Jim Nail, head of research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
